newsitem.title: USA: KLA Instruments, Tencor to merge.
newsitem.headline: KLA Instruments, Tencor to merge.

text.p: KLA Instruments Corp and Tencor Instruments said they have reached agreement to mege the two companies in a stock swap deal that would create a company with combined revenue exceeding $1 billion.
The companies said the deal, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval, will be accounted for as a pooling of interests and set up to qualify as a tax-free reorganization.

Under terms of the merger agreement, the companies said shares and options for KLA Instruments common stock will be exchanged for all outstanding shares and options of Tencor on the basis of one KLA share for each Tencor share.

The combined company, which aims to provide the most comprehensive measurement and analysis systems for yield management available to the semiconductor industry, will employ more than 3,900 people worldwide.
The companies said the definitive merger agreement had been unanimously approved by the board of directors of each company and the deal was expected to close during the quarter ending June 30, 1997.
The new company, to be called KLA-Tencor, will combine complementary product lines to create a full-line supplier of best-of-class yield management products and services.

The merger comes as semiconductor equipment stocks have been rebounding from a cyclical downturn in mid-1996, when tumbling prices for memory chips due to sharply increased capacity and insufficient demand chilled the sector.

KLA had reached a 52-week intraday high of 41-5/8 before closing at 40-7/8, up 7/8, while shares of Tencor had also hit a year intraday high of 31-1/4 in the session before closing at 30-1/2, up 7/16. The merger was announced after the close of trading in the Nasdaq market.
After hours, shares of Tencor were reported soaring as high as 37, while KLA eased as low as 39 on the news.

Analysts said the deal would create a powerhouse in the critical market for semiconductor capital equipment used for monitoring production and improving yields. That capability has become crucial in view of the surging cost of computer chipmaking plants.

"This company in their particular segment of the equipment market is just invincible," said Gus Richard, an analyst at Hambrecht and Quist. "KLA's been the dominant player, and Tencor's been a very, very strong second."
The combined company would be able to provide one-stop shopping for chip process and diagnostics equipment.

"It's one of the most rapidly growing segments of the equipment market," Richard added. "These two players are the dominant players in the market, and what's amazing is their product offerings are almost completely complementary."
Richard said the combined product offerings would enable semiconductor manufacturers to augment incremental capaicity by identifying and eliminating scrap earlier in the process.

At current prices -- with a total of 85.6 million shares outstanding after the stock swap transaction -- the deal is worth about $3.4 billion, or nearly 3.5 times revenues. Analysts said was a reasonable valuation.
Montgomery Securities analyst Brett Hodess said the deal would allow the companies to improve their distribution and to supply a "turn-key" solution for chip plants.

Analysts said executives of the companies told them in a conference call that their lawyers anticipate no regulatory hurdles, even though the companies control some 60 to 70 percent of certain markets in some areas.

KLA Chairman and Chief Executive Kenneth Levy would become chairman of KLA-Tencor, while Tencor Instruments Chairman, President and Chief Executive Jon Tompkins would serve as chief executive of the combined company.
